The opening storyStatement made. Window open.

Nick wins the rematch. Josh gets off the floor. And the injury report starts writing next week’s headlines.

CeeDees TDs did not just survive the championship rematch. Nick put up 202.10, the highest score of Week 4, and handed The People’s Champ its first loss. Ger’s 177.07 was the second-best score in the league. Sometimes you do almost everything right and still get the wrong opponent.

Chosen one. joins CeeDees at 4–0 after beating Bay Area Party Supplies. At the other end, The Comeback Kid and Loud and Stroud finally found win No. 1. Remember the raiders and Do it to them remain 0–4. Four weeks in, the standings have shape—but ten regular-season games remain, and nobody has clinched anything.

The next challenge arrives before kickoff: Lamar Jackson’s ankle, Ja’Marr Chase’s concussion protocol, and several more injury questions. The wire is thin in a 16-team dynasty league. This week, finding a usable quarterback may matter more than finding a fashionable sleeper.

Matchup of the week · the verdictNick gets the rematch.

CeeDees TDs202.104–0 after Week 4
FINAL
The People’s Champ177.073–1 after Week 4

CeeDee Lamb’s 41.40 and Kyren Williams’ 40.70 supplied 82.10 points together. Ger had real answers: Bijan Robinson scored 32.40, Puka Nacua 27.80, Jonathan Taylor 26.70 and Tucker Kraft 24.10. It still ended in a 25.03-point loss. Ger’s score would have beaten every other team in the league this week.

The voters could not separate them: four picked Ger, four picked Nick. The total was just as dramatic. Their combined 379.17 cleared last week’s 378.0 fun line by only 1.17. Five of eight ballots picked the over; three picked the under. Nick wins the game, and the over crowd gets a very narrow victory lap.

The win reinforces Nick’s early lead: 836.90 points through four weeks, 159.90 more than the next-highest total. But the Lamar injury means the league’s hottest team immediately has a superflex problem to solve.

The second featured game · the verdictThe Comeback Kid finally comes back.

The Comeback Kid123.701–3 after Week 4
FINAL
Remember the raiders73.600–4 after Week 4

Josh’s first win came by 50.10. Emanuel Wilson led with 29.00, Kirk Cousins added 24.17, and Mark Andrews supplied 17.70. The Raiders got 18.33 from Tyler Shough and 16.97 from Jordan Love, but zeroes from Jadarian Price and Kendrick Bourne left too much ground to make up.

Four of seven voters backed Josh; three backed the Raiders. The majority got both calls right: 197.30 combined points finished just 0.70 under the 198.0 line. Five ballots picked under and two picked over. The under majority nailed it—barely.

One win does not repair a season, but it changes Josh’s immediate assignment from breaking the drought to building a streak. The Raiders are still searching for that first foothold.

Around the leagueTwo nail-biters. Two first wins.

SlickBears escaped Brute Force Attack by 2.78. Loud and Stroud beat Demboyz by 3.22, with Tetairoa McMillan’s 45.30 providing a spectacular foundation for win No. 1. Chosen one. got 33.30 from Javonte Williams and 31.90 from Chuba Hubbard to stay perfect. Child Support won by 86.48, while Vick2times made it two wins on the season.

The waiver wireMore than scraps. This is your season.

The following players were confirmed available in MFFL at this edition’s check. These are targets, not completed acquisitions. In this format, prioritize a temporary starting quarterback over a speculative bench receiver.

The Beat’s MFFL-specific target board
PriorityTargetWhy / conditions
1Tyler Huntley · QBThe clearest injury replacement: would start if Lamar cannot play. First call for Nick and other teams short a superflex QB.
2Efton Chism · WRTwo catches, 42 yards and a touchdown in Week 4; an upside bench add, with playing time still the question.
WatchAthan Kaliakmanis · QBReplaced injured Mariota. Only pursue as an immediate starter if Washington confirms the job; a Daniels return could erase the opportunity.

Steve Gardner, USA TODAY via Yahoo, October 6, highlights Huntley and Chism. Ken Zalis, PressBox, October 6, also recommends Huntley.

Make room with the least useful bench stash, rather than an established starter or valuable dynasty prospect. Match the pickup to a real lineup need: Huntley offers injury cover, Chism offers a bench swing, and Kaliakmanis remains a conditional watch.

Do not treat a backup’s emergency appearance as a guaranteed job. Commanders Wire, October 6, reports that Daniels is expected back next week; wait for confirmation before counting on Kaliakmanis.

Confidence in this projected order: 25%. That is The Beat’s subjective editorial confidence in the exact eight-team order shown above, not a calculated probability or any team’s playoff odds. Confidence is low with ten regular-season games left and several major injury questions.

The strongest disagreement with the current table is the last spot: Brute Force Attack over Demboyz. Brute has scored 554.93 to Demboyz’s 538.12 despite sitting a win behind, and its opponents have piled up 686.25 points. That is a recovery case, not a free pass. Demboyz remains the first team out of this forecast and currently sits eighth by record and points.

Blue Tent All-Stars, Vick2times and bLuE BaLLeRs are also 2–2. All remain in the race, but their scoring totals trail the current top-eight group. Josh and Loud and Stroud have started their recovery at 1–3. At 0–4, Carlos and the Raiders need a run soon.
